executive_summary: Night is already postcard-grade: the fire and beam hold the top value and a storm at night is the best frame in the set. Day is not: (1) the hero is not the top value - the painted sky band and far sea (L 0.74) out-value the tower (0.62-0.65), so in a notan the Pharos merges into the horizon; (2) the water is map-pin confetti - paper-white sail roundels kept at every range since v1.4.1, burgees floating on receding masts and 469 always-on buoys give the Roads/basin 55-64 bright specks per 10k px, 7x the open sea; (3) the colour script has a 7-hour noon plateau, a magenta-violet dusk and a pool-cyan basin that ignores the hour's light. A real defect: the 3D mainland mesh ('shakkei') leaks in front of the camera-attached sky card whenever the camera stands back - zoom past ~700 m on any desktop, every landing on screens squarer than ~1.2, tablet portrait. Best value for cost: retire that mesh, a day value lock, tonal roundels plus quieter buoys, a night stale-fog that reads, and a 'last light on the Pharos' dusk moment.
current_state: Night is the benchmark: lantern L 0.70 vs sky 0.22-0.41, calm beam, lamp pools and moon glade (base-night, O1-notan-day-golden-night bottom row); psi=none reads as a dark lantern; DEWS DANGER reads as weather by day and is superb at night (O1-storm-night).

16:10 composition is sound (Pharos on the left third, civic quarter balancing right, basin and mole as leading lines); ultrawide and small-laptop hold up; the Roads (top right) are the densest clutter in every frame.
Day value structure is inverted: the brightest mass is the sky + far-sea band; the stated intent 'the Pharos holds the top value' (src/harbour/ocean/sea-tone.ts:6-7) is met only from sunset on.

Skies are the best day asset (dawn, 7:45, golden distinct and painterly) but the basin stays cyan/teal under all of them: the sea body is unlit (src/harbour/ocean/ocean-material.ts:200-279), the hour reaches it only via hbSeaGolden on sunlit water at low sun (src/harbour/ocean/sea-golden.ts:8-22).
Speckle density (blobs dL>0.10 over a 9 px median, base-day): Roads 64/10k px, basin 55, open sea beyond the mouth 8.7 (O1-noise-crops).

5-second data read: DEWS storm strong; stale fog strong by day (basin chroma -68 %), nearly invisible at night; PSI legible at night only (by day a rhythm glint, rarely in a still); off-peg sea subtle; Shoals clear; Wreck Cove only at the overview in the tilt-shift soft zone.

Horizon = camera-attached painted card (src/harbour/sky/sky-system.ts:19-23, BAND_FRAC 0.2 at :75): elegant at 16:10, but its distance rule lets the 3D mainland through on zoom-out and squarer screens.

REVIEW.md 1-15: 8 fixed (1, 2, 4, 5, 9, 12, 13, 14), 1 fixed but changed character (11: basin now the most saturated mass), 4 partly open (3, 6, 8, 15), 7 partly fixed (cones legible, office works not discernible at heart), 10 unverified (summer only).

findings.title: 3D mainland mesh breaks the horizon on zoom-out and on squarer screens
findings.evidence: shots/O1-zoomout-1100.png (16:10, cam=-110.31,20,-98.99,1100,26), base-tablet-portrait.png, O1-portrait-overview.png; src/harbour/sky/sky-system.ts:379-392; src/harbour/world/island-system.ts:56-57; scripts/harbour/blender/island/hb_dress.py:1575-1637; compose.py:1182-1192; hb_export.py:324-328; src/harbour/world/aerial.ts:16
findings.detail: The sky card sits at R = camY / tan(pitch - 0.3*vfov) so the pretend horizon is 20 % below the frame top; R grows with camera height. The 'shakkei' node (mainland ~520 m NW of the island, 3,966 tris) only loses castShadow and gets the generic aerial tint capped at 0.28, not the 'strong fog' its export note asks for. Modelled with the real framing code: the default 16:10 heart hides it by only 22 m (R 911 m vs coast 933 m); at the heart pitch any zoom >= ~700 m (max 1150 m) puts it in front of the card; landings on aspect <= ~1.2 (square 808 m, foldable 902 m, tablet portrait 1089 m; tablet-portrait overview 1547 m) show it at once. It renders as a faceted brown/green wall with pale triangle facets at its foot filling the top quarter.
findings.fix: Hide the node at runtime (island-system.ts:57: visible=false, drop from staticDepth) or stop exporting it; the painted shakkei ridges (sky-glsl.ts:348-371) already carry the hills. Add a framing test over aspect 0.75-2.4 x zoom to maxDistance asserting no runtime mesh lies between the island bounds and R. (Idea O1-I3.)

findings.title: Day hierarchy inverted: the Pharos is not the top value
findings.evidence: shots/O1-notan-day-golden-night.png; measured L: base-day tower top 0.65 / shaft 0.62 vs sky beside lantern 0.74 and far sea 0.74; golden 0.68 vs 0.70; winter 0.66 vs 0.78-0.80; src/harbour/sky/sky-glsl.ts:130-132; src/harbour/engine/time-of-day.ts:97,104,110; src/harbour/ocean/ocean-material.ts:295,521
findings.detail: The visible sky band is only ~5 deg tall at the heart pitch, and the gradient t = e/6.5 leaves the sky at lantern height ~40 % zenith plus a horizon lift, so it stays near the near-white day horizon (#E8F1F4 at noon). The far sea is lifted by the haze ramp from 0.62 R and by Fresnel reflection of that pale horizon. In a 2-value notan the tower merges into the bright top band; only from sunset on does the lantern lead.
findings.fix: Deepen the band (e/4.5, horizon lift below 1 deg only), lower day horizon/haze keys ~8 %, start the far-sea haze at 0.72 R, lift the limewash ~5 %; accept when tower lit face >= band behind +0.05 L at t=9/11/14.5/16.4 and in winter (value study: shots/O1-study-hero-value.png). (O1-I1.)

ideas.title: Hero value lock by day
ideas.what: (1) sky-glsl.ts:130-132: gradient t = clamp(e/4.5) (was 6.5) and the near-horizon lift only below 1 deg (smoothstep(0,1,e), 0.25) so the visible 5-deg band reaches mid-blue behind the lantern; (2) day keys ~8 % darker: 8.5 h horizon #E6EEF0->#D9E4EA, haze #C2D3DC->#B4C8D3; 12 h horizon #E8F1F4->#D8E5EC, haze #BCD3DF->#AEC5D3; 16 h horizon #F2E6D6->#E6DACB (time-of-day.ts:97,104,110); (3) far-sea haze from 0.72 R (ocean-material.ts:521, was 0.62); (4) Pharos limewash albedo +5 %. Acceptance on real-GPU frames: tower lit face >= band behind the lantern +0.05 L at t=9/11/14.5/16.4 and winter, and the tower separates in a 2-value notan (target structure: shots/O1-study-hero-value.png, a PIL value study: sky 0.74->0.61, far sea 0.74->0.65).

ideas.data_and_dom: n/a: time-of-day palette only. Stale fog becomes more distinct (its milky lift contrasts with a deeper clear sky); the aerial tint (reads uHaze) darkens slightly but stays static and data-independent.
ideas.where: src/harbour/sky/sky-glsl.ts:130-132; src/harbour/engine/time-of-day.ts:94-112; src/harbour/ocean/ocean-material.ts:521; src/harbour/world/materials.ts (Pharos kit albedo)

ideas.title: Coins as print, not pins
ideas.what: fleet-material.ts:399-421: derive the roundel's screen diameter from its existing derivatives; pin = 1 - smoothstep(6, 16, discPx); below ~16 px the paper-white FIELD of the disc (atlas pixels near paper white) falls to the cloth tone x1.1 while the logo ink and the brand ring stay; full paper-white roundel whenever vFleetMisc.x > 0 (hover/selected/searched). ideas.title: Colour script v2 (three new keys + a sea that follows the hour)
ideas.what: Retune time-of-day.ts keys and add three: 3.0 'quiet watch' (zenith #03061A, horizon #121A2E, windowOcc 0.1, lamp 40, exposure 0.40), 7.5 'silver morning' (zenith #4E7FC0, horizon #E2E9EE), 14.5 'warm afternoon' (zenith #5482C0, horizon #EDE6DA, warmSat 1.1); dawn blueSat 0.9->0.8; dusk 19.7 haze #857288->#6E7890 and hemiSky/ambient #56689E->#4E66A0 (warm/cool split, not magenta); blue hour horizon cooler (#2E3C68). Add optional TimeKeyframe fields seaTint (hex) and seaChroma (0..1), applied to the sea body before the Shoals reef mix (ocean-material.ts:257-264) so the basin is slate-lilac at first light, clear cyan-teal (not pool-cyan) at 7:30, jade at golden, low-chroma teal at dusk. Hero dL targets per key (report table).

ideas.data_and_dom: n/a: time of day is decorative. Off-peg chop, DEWS wind layers and the Shoals' turquoise are untouched (tint applied before the reef mix).

ideas.risks: The seasonal remap compresses windows in winter (check Nov and Jun); judge every key on npm run preview frames, never SwiftShader.

ideas.title: Last light on the Pharos (the Earth-shadow line)
ideas.what: In the kit key-light term (world/materials.ts, inherited by the fleet) multiply the sun's direct light by smoothstep(h-6, h+6, worldY), with h = mix(-10, 130, smoothstep(0.10, 0.0, uSunDir.y)) while the sun is low and uNight < 0.5: over the last ~25 min before sunset the shadow climbs quays, roofs and masts, the lantern, statue and mirror keep the gold last, then the PSI fire takes over as uNight rises. Dawn mirrors it: the first ray touches the lantern.
ideas.visitor_benefit: A quiet, physically true daily moment that hands the light from the sun to the fire and makes the lighthouse the last lit thing.
ideas.data_and_dom: n/a: hour only; fire and beam keep their PSI mapping; legend 'time of day'.
ideas.where: src/harbour/world/materials.ts (key light); src/harbour/fleet/fleet-material.ts (inherits kit); src/harbour/engine/time-of-day.ts (sun elevation)
ideas.perf_cost: ~2-3 ALU in kit and fleet fragments; 0 draws
ideas.risks: Must not read as a data cue (daily, solar-timed); a pure function of the hour, so reduced motion is unaffected; check against the sun shadow map at grazing sun (t=17.0-17.2 in November).

ideas.title: Night fog that reads
ideas.what: With the existing stale fog on (fog amount, readings/fog.ts:92) and night > 0, scale by fogAmount x night: bloom radius 0.72->0.9 and intensity +0.5 (post.ts:237,331), light-sprite halo x2 and core -20 % (lights-system.ts:164-171), far riding/anchor lights fade by exp(-od) using the fog pass's optical-depth formula (fog.ts:35-45), the beam sheath scatter x1.5 with reach and colour unchanged (beam-system.ts:404-414); halos desaturated 30 % so it reads grey-veiled, not festive.

ideas.data_and_dom: Same signal: endpoint landmark state 'stale' -> out.fog (readings/bind.ts:296-299) -> fog amount; threshold unchanged; DOM unchanged (header freshness pill 'stale - 2 h old', ledger 'fog means the data has gone stale'). Unit test: night + fog -> bloom/halo multipliers > 1 and riding-light extinction > 0; fog off or day -> identity.
ideas.perf_cost: ~0: bloom already runs; +3 ALU per light sprite; no new pass
ideas.risks: Keep it calm and grey (no glow spectacle); keep it distinct from DEWS storm (storm = slate deck + rain; fog = halos + extinction); static, so reduced motion is unaffected.

ideas.what: Drive the lantern fire's glow (not the beam's reach or length) with max(nightK, 0.6*gloom) (beam-system.ts:341-348, beam/fire.ts; gloom from the weather director, sky-system.ts WeatherSkyLike.gloom) so a lit Pharos shows its fire through a dark DEWS storm by day; add a faint cool sky-rim on the tower's sky-facing edges when storm > 0.5 (world/materials.ts). ideas.what: A repo script (scripts/harbour/art-check.mjs) over real-GPU review frames from npm run preview / shot.mjs at t=3/6.9/9/11/14.5/16.4/17.1/17.6/22 plus DANGER, stale and winter: (a) tower-vs-band dL from the layout-projected Pharos box (warn by day if < +0.05), (b) speckle density in the Roads and basin (warn > 35/10k px), (c) basin chroma per hour, (d) horizon intrusion: no non-sky pixels above the pretend horizon except the Pharos and smoke, for 4 aspects x 3 zooms, (e) the colour-script strip for the release review.
